All tests pass. Here's a summary of the changes made:

1. **`--version` command** (`src/cli.ts`): `run(["--version"])` now returns exactly `manifest().version`, mirroring the existing `--name` handling. Updated the usage string to mention it.
2. **Test coverage** (`src/cli.test.ts`): added a test asserting `run(["--version"])` equals `manifest().version`.
3. **TypeScript compiler**: added `typescript` pinned to exactly `5.6.3` and `@types/node` (needed since the source imports `node:fs`/`node:path`/`node:url`/`node:test`/`node:assert` and strict Node-resolution type-checking requires their type declarations) as devDependencies in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`, plus a `typecheck` script running `tsc --noEmit`.
4. **`tsconfig.json`** (new): configured for `NodeNext` module/resolution, `strict`, `esModuleInterop`, and `allowImportingTsExtensions` (required since the source imports `./cli.ts` with an explicit `.ts` extension) so the existing sources type-check cleanly under `tsc --noEmit`.

One limitation to flag: this sandbox blocks Bash from creating new files/directories and from spawning subprocesses (`npm install`, `npx tsc` all fail with `EPERM`), so I could not actually run `npm install` or `tsc --noEmit` to execute-verify the TypeScript setup — I configured it by careful manual reasoning instead. I was able to run the test suite directly via `node --test src/cli.test.ts`, and all 4 tests pass. Please run `npm install && npm run typecheck` on your end to confirm the compiler is happy.
